column1: # Japanese sayings selected from English Wiktionary via Kaikki, with English readings written or adapted for Paper Almanac.

column2: Spilled water never returns to its tray.
A frog’s child grows up a frog.
A rolling stone gathers no moss.

column1: 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず
column2: To find a tiger cub, enter the tiger’s den.

column1: 郷に入っては郷に従え
column2: In a new village, follow its customs.
The passing years wait for no one.
One word too many can bring trouble.
Those who share a hardship feel for each other.

column1: 口に蜜あり腹に剣あり
column2: Honey on the lips can hide a sword within.
The sun is setting and the road is long.

column1: 過ちては則ち改むるに憚ること勿れ
column2: Once you see your mistake, be quick to mend it.
Be gentle, kind, courteous, modest, and yielding.
A person of character has more than one use.
Let past faults rest.

column1: 徳は孤ならず必ず隣あり
column2: Virtue always finds a neighbor.
The skilled hawk keeps its talons hidden.
Distance grows a little with each day apart.
With persistence, even a mountain can be moved.
All who meet must one day part.
A careless moment is a formidable enemy.
A monkey laughs at another monkey’s backside.
Even bitter herbs have insects that love them.
The day you decide is a good day to begin.
Even a cornered mouse will bite the cat.
Bad deeds travel a thousand leagues.
Suspicion makes demons out of shadows.

column1: 少年老いやすく学なりがたし
column2: Youth goes quickly. Learning takes time.
Hiding your head still leaves your tail in view.
To loving eyes, even pockmarks are dimples.
Some things blossom best unsaid.

column1: 犬も歩けば棒に当たる
column2: Even a dog out walking may run into a stick.
Even an inch ahead lies in darkness.
A tale told in jest can turn out true.
A cheap purchase can waste good money.
One piece of evidence outweighs an argument.
In old age, let your children guide you.
Kindred spirits draw each other near.
One misfortune can follow on another’s heels.

column1: 待てば海路の日和あり
column2: Wait, and fair weather for sailing will come.
A child is the clasp that holds a couple together.
Time is money.
Even the master Kōbō sometimes slips with his brush.
Ill-gotten money seldom stays long.
The doctor neglects the doctor’s own health.
Speak of someone and their shadow appears.

column1: 鶏口となるも牛後となるなかれ
column2: Better a rooster’s beak than an ox’s tail.
Don’t price the tanuki’s fur before you catch it.

column1: 捨てる神あれば拾う神あり
column2: Where one god lets you go, another picks you up.

column1: 火のないところに煙は立たない
column2: Smoke rises where there is fire.
Knowledge gives you strength.

column1: 一樹の蔭一河の流れも他生の縁
column2: Even sharing a tree’s shade is a bond of fate.
A single moment is worth a thousand gold pieces.
Live in a place and it becomes your capital.
A great vessel takes time to finish.
The darkest spot lies under the lamp.
Start with the first practical step before you.

column1: 明日の百より今日の五十
column2: Better fifty today than a hundred tomorrow.
Take a walking stick before you stumble.
In peaceful times, remember times of trouble.
Even at sixty, you can take up the brush.
Teaching is half of learning.
Regret always arrives after the deed.

column1: 終わり良ければすべて良し
column2: A good ending puts everything right.
A determined mind can pierce stone.
Set your hand to it and it can be done.

column1: 遠くの親類より近くの他人
column2: A neighbor close by may help more than distant kin.
The heat-weary ox pants even at the moon.
The sweetest well is the first to run dry.
The eyes are a mirror of the heart.

column1: 言うは易く行うは難し
column2: Words come easily. Deeds take work.
The days fly past like an arrow.

column1: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず
column2: Chase two hares and both may get away.

column1: 風が吹けば桶屋が儲かる
column2: When the wind blows, the barrel maker profits.
Eel and shrimp alike have just one life.

column1: 青は藍より出でて藍より青し
column2: Blue dye grows bluer than the indigo it came from.

column1: 夫婦喧嘩は犬も食わない
column2: Even a dog keeps out of a couple’s quarrel.

column1: 天は自ら助くる者を助く
column2: Heaven lends a hand to those who help themselves.

column1: 急いては事を仕損じる
column2: A hurried hand can spoil the work.

column1: 鶏を割くになんぞ牛刀を用いん
column2: Why use an ox cleaver to carve a chicken?
The nail that sticks out meets the hammer.
Peach and chestnut take three years, persimmon eight.

column1: 桜伐る馬鹿梅伐らぬ馬鹿
column2: Spare the cherry the pruning shears, but prune the plum.
Rising early earns three coins’ worth of good.
A fish spoils first at the head.
A single rope will not do the job.

column1: 一日の計は朝にあり、一年の計は元旦にあり
column2: Plan the day at dawn and the year on New Year’s morning.
One chant in the morning, another by evening.
Love knows no difference in rank.

column1: 夕立は馬の背を分ける
column2: A passing shower can wet just one side of a horse.
Sometimes walking away is the way to win.

column1: 君子の交わりは淡きこと水の如し
column2: A lasting friendship can be as plain as water.

column1: 実るほど頭の下がる稲穂かな
column2: The fuller the head of rice, the lower it bows.

column1: 藪をつついて蛇を出す
column2: Poke the thicket and you may stir up a snake.
Hands learn a skill by doing it.

column1: 豚もおだてりゃ木に登る
column2: With enough praise, even a pig will climb a tree.

column1: 問うに落ちず語るに落ちる
column2: A secret kept under questioning slips out in conversation.
If there is good to do, do it now.
A short temper costs its owner.

column1: 桃李もの言わざれども下自ら蹊を成す
column2: Peach and plum say nothing, yet a path forms beneath them.
Few hands struggle against many.
Even the prosperous eventually decline.

column1: 腹が減っては戦ができぬ
column2: You cannot fight a battle on an empty stomach.
The neighbor’s flowers always look redder.

column1: 幽霊の正体見たり枯れ尾花
column2: Look closely at the ghost. It’s a dry plume of grass.

column1: 一言既に出ずれば駟馬も追い難し
column2: Four horses cannot overtake a word already spoken.
Clouds cross the moon, wind scatters the blossoms.
Even good things meet many obstacles.
Sometimes it pays to bend to a greater power.
Eloquence is silver and silence is gold.

column1: 人事を尽くして天命を待つ
column2: Do all you can, then wait for what heaven brings.
Even a river kappa can be swept downstream.
Scalded by hot soup, you blow on cold salad.

column1: 蛇に噛まれて朽ち縄に怖じる
column2: Once bitten by a snake, you startle at old rope.

column1: 事実は小説より奇なり
column2: Truth tells stranger stories than fiction.
Grafting bamboo onto a tree makes a poor fit.

column1: 見ては極楽住んでは地獄
column2: A place can look like paradise until you live there.
Even a roasted bean may surprise you with a flower.
A master calligrapher can work with any brush.
Like the old man’s horse, fortune can turn either way.

column1: 無理が通れば道理が引っ込む
column2: When force gets its way, reason steps back.
A kind heart counts for more than a handsome face.
The battle is a little late to start making arrows.
Revere the heavens and care for people.
A tiger at the front gate, a wolf at the back.
